measures.title: Amendment to the Nevada Constitution (Initiative Petition C-05-2023): Right to Abortion
measures.summary: This citizen initiative would add a fundamental right to an abortion to the Nevada Constitution, protected from interference by state or local governments when performed by a qualified health care professional until fetal viability, or at any point when needed to protect the pregnant patient's life or health. Government could restrict the right only for a compelling state interest, meaning the least restrictive way to protect the patient's health consistent with accepted clinical standards. Voters approved it in 2024; it must pass again in 2026 to take effect.
measures.yesMeans: You approve adding a constitutional right to abortion to the Nevada Constitution, as voters also did in 2024.
measures.noMeans: The Nevada Constitution stays as it is; abortion remains legal under existing state law (generally up to 24 weeks), which the Legislature could change.

measures.title: Amendment to the Nevada Constitution (Initiative Petition C-02-2023): Voter Identification
measures.summary: This citizen initiative would amend the Nevada Constitution to require in-person voters to show an approved photo ID, such as a Nevada driver's license, state or federal ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal ID, or Nevada public college student ID. Mail voters would have to provide the last four digits of their Nevada driver's license or Social Security number (or the number assigned at registration) to verify their identity. Voters approved it in 2024; if approved again in 2026, the changes would take effect for the 2028 election cycle.
measures.yesMeans: You approve adding photo ID for in-person voting and ID-number verification for mail voting to the Nevada Constitution.
measures.noMeans: The Nevada Constitution stays as it is, and voters would generally not have to show ID to vote except in the limited situations current law requires.
